title: activation-and-lifecycle-tool-matrix-playbook-2024
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the activation and lifecycle of the primary internal tools new and existing employees need to be productive at Redwood. It ties together: role and ladder expectations, benefits enrollment touchpoints, hiring/onboarding checklists, and the minimal set of internal tools with ownership and access instructions. The intent is to give hiring managers, people-ops partners, and team leads a single reference for end-to-end new-joiner activation and ongoing lifecycle changes.

Who should use this
- People managers and hiring managers
- People-ops and IT onboarding specialists
- Team leads and onboarding buddies
- Individual contributors requesting role changes or benefits corrections

Scope and constraints
- Covers corporate (non-customer-facing) toolset and core infra access patterns. Does not cover deep production infra runbooks (see eng-infra) or customer-specific SSO exceptions.
- Applicable to full-time, part-time, and contractor employment statuses unless stated.

Quick reference: tool matrix
| Tool | Purpose | Primary owner | Default access group | Onboarding step | Deprovision trigger |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Okta | SSO identity + MFA | Identity & Security | all-employees | 1 - Invitation + MFA setup | offboarding completed |
| Slack | Team communications | IT Comms | workspace:redwood | 2 - Workspace join | offboarding completed |
| G Suite (email, drive) | Email & docs | IT Operations | gmail-enabled | 2 - Email and Drive share | offboarding completed |
| Jira | Ticketing, project tracking | Eng PMs | redwood-staff | 3 - Project board access + role | role exit or team change |
| Confluence | Internal docs | People Ops | internal-read | 3 - Space permissions set | role exit or space revocation |
| Github (org) | Code + infra | Eng Platform | engineers | 4 - GitHub team invite | IAM change or offboarding |
| Linear / Asana | Product work tracking | Product Ops | product-team | 3 - Project invite | offboarding |
| 1Password | Secrets and credentials | Security | credential-access | 2 - Vault onboarding | deprovision workflow |
| Okta-managed AWS roles | Cloud dev/test access | Cloud Infra | cloud-dev | 4 - IAM role assignment | role revocation |
| Benefits Portal | Enrollment, paystubs | People Ops | employee | 1 - Benefits enrollment email | termination or benefits-eligibility change |

Matrix notes:
- Column definitions: 'Onboarding step' maps to the recommended step order during a new-hire 1-30 day activation.
- 'Deprovision trigger' lists the primary event that should remove access; for contractors the People Ops checklist has additional mid-contract checkpoints.

Activation checklist (first 7 days)
1. Pre-day-1 (People Ops): initiate Okta invite and benefits portal account (owner: People Ops).
2. Day 0 / Day 1: Employee accepts Okta invite, sets MFA (Authenticator + YubiKey optional), confirm email and calendar provisioning.
3. Day 1: Slack workspace join; onboarding channel assignment; assign onboarding buddy.
4. Day 2: GitHub organization invite (for engineers) or project tool invites (PMs, Design).
5. Day 3–5: 1Password onboarding and secrets vault orientation (security training required).
6. Day 5–7: Confluence space access granted; completion of required short training modules (Code of Conduct, Security Foundations, Data Handling).

Sample CLI snippet to validate GitHub invite (engineering onboarding)
$ gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" /user/memberships/orgs/redwood | jq .state
# expected output: \"active\"

Role ladder touchpoints and tool consequences
- IC levels (IC1 - IC6): access to repos, staging stacks, and deploy pipelines increases at IC3 and IC5. Stage gating requires manager sign-off and security approval for elevated roles.
- Engineering on-call privileges: granted at IC3+ after documented runbook review and on-call training. On-call access includes pager duty integration and ops alerts subscription.
- People Ops / HR elevated tasks (benefits adjustments, payroll exceptions): require two approvers (people-ops lead + finance approver) for changes that affect compensation.

Role change procedure (promotion, lateral move, level change)
1. Manager initiates role-change form in Confluence > People Ops forms and attaches updated role profile, proposed compensation impact, and eligible start date.
2. People Ops reviews, routes to Finance for comp verification (target SLA: 3 business days).
3. Upon approval, IT and Identity are notified automatically to adjust Okta groups and GitHub teams.
4. Manager confirms tooling access changes with the employee and updates onboarding checklist to reflect new permissions.

Benefits & perks — activation and correction flows
- Standard benefit categories: medical, dental, vision, commuter, fitness stipend, home office stipend, retirement 401(k) matching.
- Enrollment window: first 30 days after start. Late enrollments require HR case and may have carrier-based restrictions.
- Corrections: Submit benefits-correction form (link in the People Ops space). People Ops SLA: 5 business days for enrollment changes, 15 business days for payroll corrections.

Access request and emergency escalation
- Standard requests: use the Self-Service Access form in Confluence (owner: IT Ops). Expect 2–3 business days for normal requests.
- Emergency access (e.g., urgent cloud access for P1 incident): manager must page Security On-Call and People Ops; include the justification, time-bound window, and required owner to revoke access.
- Audit trail: every access change is logged in Okta and 1Password for 90 days by default; teams needing extended retention should request it via security-exceptions@redwood.com.

Onboarding training map (minimum required within 30 days)
- Day 1: Code of Conduct, Privacy & Data Handling (30 min each)
- Week 1: Security Foundations (1 hour) + 1Password essentials (30 min)
- Week 2: Role-specific tooling walkthrough (mentor-led)
- Month 1: Role proficiency check-in (manager + peer)

Tool retirement and lifecycle changes
- When deprecating an internal tool, Product of Record must publish a migration plan and a minimum 60-day notice to all consumers. Migration plan must include: data export strategy, access impacts, and training sessions.
- Legacy credentials: rotate and revoke at decommission time; update the matrix and publish a short deprecation FAQ.

Common troubleshooting and FAQs
Q: I joined but didn’t receive the Okta invite. What do I do?
A: Check spam, then contact people-ops@redwood.com with your start date and full name. People Ops will re-issue in 1 business day.
Q: My benefits elections are wrong after the first payroll.
A: Submit a benefits-correction form and cc your manager. Payroll runs weekly; expect up to 2 cycles for adjustments to appear.

Ownership and escalation contacts
- People Ops (onboarding owner): people-ops@redwood.com
- Identity & Security (Okta, 1Password): identity-security@redwood.com
- IT Operations (Slack, G Suite): it-ops@redwood.com
- Eng Platform (GitHub org, CI access): eng-platform@redwood.com

Appendix: sample access request template (paste into Confluence request)
Title: [Access Request] <Tool> - <Purpose>
Employee: <Full name> | Role: <Current role> | Manager: <Manager name>
Requested groups/permissions: <list>
Business justification: <why>
Requested duration: <permanent|time-boxed YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD>
Approvals: Manager: <name> | People Ops: <name>
